description.para: This parameter selects how much of an outage SMB3 Persistent Handles are expected to survive. It only has an effect if is enabled and Samba is clustered.

With full_outage, the default, Samba additionally maintains a persistent backup copy of the handle state in a second, persistent ctdb database. Handles then also survive an outage of every node at the same time, planned or unplanned: a maintenance window in which the whole cluster is shut down and restarted loses the volatile databases, and the handle state is restored from the backup when the cluster comes back.

With partial_outage, that backup database is not used. Handles survive any outage that leaves at least one node running, which covers a node crash, a rolling restart, and the loss of all but one node, because the handle state is kept on every node of the cluster. Handles are lost if every node is down at the same time.

The backup database is not free. Every change to the state of a persistent handle costs an additional cluster wide transaction, and that transaction is written to stable storage on every node, so it involves an fsync per node. Sites that do not need handles to survive a full cluster shutdown can set partial_outage and avoid that cost.
